title.narrative: Stengthening public opinion research for Univeristy Social Outreach

description.narrative: The project aims to strengthen independent research on public opinion in El Salvador in order to better understand how citizens perceive key social, political, and environmental issues. In recent years, the country has experienced major political and social changes. While many citizens express support for government security policies, there is also growing distrust toward democratic institutions and traditional political representation. Environmental and social challenges are affecting vulnerable communities and systematic data about how citizens perceive these issues is limited. To address this gap, the project will support the work of the University Institute of Public Opinion (IUDOP) providing direct evidence on citizens’ perceptions of key national issues such as democracy, elections, environmental sustainability, and the broader social reality of the country. By producing rigorous and accessible research, the project seeks to contribute to more informed public debate and decision-making. The expected change is that institutions, CSOs, and the wider public will have access to reliable information aimed to transparent dialogue, democratic participation, and critical reflection about national issues. These changes will be achieved through four main strategies: research, training, analysis, and knowledge exchange. Results will be widely disseminated through reports, public events, and accessible multimedia materials.
